ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

1	# AGENTS.md — Operating Rules for AI Agents in MythosMini
2	
3	MythosMini is a small language model ("mini Fable") built in Python 3.12. This file is the contract for any agent working here. Read it fully, then read `journal.md` before starting any task. Detailed procedures live in `docs/rules/` — read the relevant one before doing that kind of work; they are part of this contract, not optional extras.
4	
5	## Commands
6	
7	```bash
8	make setup    # create .venv and install pinned dependencies (idempotent)
9	make test     # run the full test suite: pytest tests/ -v
10	make lint     # ruff format --check + ruff check + mypy --strict on src/ and tests/
11	make fix      # ruff format + ruff check --fix (apply formatting)
12	make run      # run the application entry point
13	make pyaot    # run pyaot on the entire project (python pyaot.py .)
14	```
15	
16	These five entry points must always work with no arguments and no manual configuration. If your change affects setup, running, or testing, update the Makefile in the same session and re-run the affected target to prove it still works.
17	
18	## Session Workflow
19	
20	Follow these steps in order for every task:
21	
22	1. Read `journal.md` — the entire file, every entry in full. Note any past failures or open items relevant to your task; never retry a recorded failed approach unchanged.
23	2. Look up the functions you will touch in `docs/functions.md`.
24	3. Prove any new piece (function, dependency, algorithm) in an isolated test under `tests/` before integrating it into source files. Details: `docs/rules/testing.md`.
25	4. Make the change, following the code rules below.
26	5. Run `make lint` and `make test`. Both must pass clean.
27	6. Run `make pyaot` on the entire project directory. If false-positives occur, edit `pyaot.py` to suppress them (adjust type narrowers, annotation inference, or built-in knowledge); never silence a true positive. Repeat until clean.
28	7. Update `docs/functions.md` for every function added, changed, or removed. Details: `docs/rules/documentation.md`.
29	8. Write a `journal.md` entry using the template in `docs/rules/journal.md`. Also journal mid-task whenever you finish a meaningful unit or abandon an approach — not only at the end.
30	9. Review `git diff`; revert any line not required by the task.
31	10. Commit in small units with short plain messages. Details: `docs/rules/process.md`.
32	11. Run the final checklist at the bottom of this file.
33	
34	## Boundaries
35	
36	| ✅ Always | ⚠️ Ask the user first | 🚫 Never |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| Write real, complete, working implementations | Editing files outside the task's scope | Placeholder values, stub functions, TODO/FIXME markers |
39	| Run `make lint` and `make test` before declaring done | Deleting source files or functions the task didn't call for | Comments or docstrings in source code |
40	| Document every function in `docs/functions.md` | Upgrading or adding a dependency mid-task | Bare `except:` or silently swallowed errors |
41	| Journal frequently with the full template | Revisiting an approach `journal.md` records as failed | `# type: ignore`, lint-ignore directives, skipped or weakened tests |
42	| Commit each working unit as you go | Anything irreversible (force-push, history rewrite, data deletion) | Secrets or absolute paths in code; secrets in git |
43	| Prove new code in `tests/` before integration | Restructuring `tests/`, `docs/`, or the Makefile | Reporting success with failing or unrun tests |
44	
45	## Code Rules
46	
47	**Real implementations only.** Every value, function, and config you write is the actual final version. No `YOUR_API_KEY`, no `example.com`, no `pass` bodies, no "replace this later". If you lack information only the user has (a credential, a decision), stop and ask rather than inventing a stand-in. Before finishing a file, search it for `TODO`, `FIXME`, `placeholder`, and stub bodies.
48	
49	**No comments — document in `docs/functions.md` instead.** Source code carries meaning through names and structure alone. Every function gets a full entry in `docs/functions.md` (purpose, parameters, returns, side effects, failure modes, callers/callees, last-modified). Add the entry when you add the function, update it when you change it, delete it when you delete it — same session. Entry format and a complete example: `docs/rules/documentation.md`.
50	
51	**Fully typed.** Every parameter, return value, and class attribute is annotated. `mypy --strict` passes with zero errors on everything you touch. Avoid `Any`; where it is genuinely unavoidable, explain why in the function's doc entry. Fix type errors rather than suppressing them.
52	
53	**Small and flat.** Functions stay under ~40 lines and 3 levels of nesting. Use guard clauses and extraction. If a function's honest name needs the word "and", split it. Extracted helpers get doc entries and test coverage like any function.
54	
55	**Naming.** Match the existing codebase conventions first. Where none exist: `snake_case` for functions, variables, and files; `PascalCase` for classes; `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` for constants. Names state intent precisely:
56	
57	```python
58	def retry_failed_uploads(pending_jobs: list[UploadJob], timeout_seconds: float) -> list[UploadJob]:
59	```
60	
61	not `def process2(data, t):`. Booleans read as predicates (`is_ready`), collections are plural, units go in the name when ambiguous.
62	
63	**No dead code.** In files you are working on, delete unused imports, variables, unreachable branches, and functions with zero callers (verify with a repo-wide grep first). Git history is the archive — note the last commit hash in `journal.md` if it might be wanted again. Dead code in files outside your task is a journal finding, not a deletion.
64	
65	**Fail loud.** Catch only specific exceptions you can genuinely handle. Don't return `None` or empty defaults to paper over a failure the caller needs to know about. Validate inputs at boundaries (CLI args, file contents, network responses) and fail there with a message stating what was expected and what was received. Every failure mode you introduce is documented in the function's doc entry and exercised by a test where practical.
66	
67	**No hardcoded paths or secrets.** Secrets come from environment variables or a git-ignored `.env`; if a real secret is needed and unavailable, ask the user. Paths are computed relative to the repository root. Tunable values (paths, ports, model hyperparameters, thresholds) live in one config module with defaults sane enough that `make run` and `make test` work untouched.
68	
69	## Testing Rules
70	
71	The codebase is the expensive PC; `tests/` is the trash PC you try parts on first. Nothing unproven gets installed in the expensive one.
72	
73	**Sandbox first.** Before a new function, dependency, or algorithm lands in a source file: write a test in `tests/` that exercises it in isolation with real inputs and real assertions, run it, see it pass, then integrate. This applies even to one-liners you are sure about. If the isolated test fails, the source tree stays untouched while you iterate in `tests/`, journaling failed attempts.
74	
75	**E2E on everything.** Every change — however small — gets an end-to-end test that exercises the real entry point with real inputs, plus a real run of the suite (`make test`), with the actual output recorded in the journal. Unit tests are welcome additions, never substitutes. Failing tests mean the task is not done: fix the code, or journal the exact failure state and report it. Never delete, skip, or weaken a test to make it pass.
76	
77	**Tests are permanent and committed.** Isolated proving tests go in `tests/`, end-to-end suites in `tests/e2e/`. They are regression evidence, not scratch files. Full procedure: `docs/rules/testing.md`.
78	
79	## Scope Rules
80	
81	Touch only the files and lines the task requires. Needing to edit `batch.py` is not license to refactor, reformat, or "clean up" `LR.py` or anything else. Before editing a file, check its dependents via the callers/callees in `docs/functions.md`; after editing, the tests prove dependents still work. No drive-by renames, reformatting of untouched code, dependency bumps, or deletions outside the task. If an out-of-scope problem genuinely blocks you, journal it and ask the user before touching it. The `git diff` review in step 8 is where you catch and revert scope creep.
82	
83	## Training Script Change Rules
84	
85	Whenever you edit the training script (`train.py` or anything under `src/mythosmini/`) to change training behavior, you MUST run a full 2B-token test for that change before it is accepted: `python3 train.py 2 4`, end to end through benchmarking and SLERP. One feature per test — never add two things and then test, because you will not know what did what. Each feature gets its own change, its own 2B-token run, and its own row in `scores.md` recording the commit ID, what was done, whether it is being kept or reverted, a description, and the resulting benchmark scores. A change without its 2B-token test result in `scores.md` is not done.
86	
87	## Process Rules
88	
89	**Commits:** commit after every small unit that leaves the repo working — many per session, never one big one at the end. Committing is your default behavior; do not wait for the user to ask. Messages are one line, lowercase, plain, stating what changed:
90	
91	```
92	fix off-by-one in batch loader
93	add e2e test for tokenizer round-trip
94	```
95	
96	No prefixes, no bullet lists, no bodies, no trailers, no emoji. Never commit a known-broken state without marking it (`wip: parser broken on empty input`) and fixing it in the next commits.
97	
98	**Dependencies:** exact pins only (`torch==2.9.1`), in `requirements.txt`. Adding one means: pin the version you tested, update `make setup`, journal why it was needed. Prefer the standard library when it does the job. Upgrades are their own explicit task, never a side effect.
99	
100	**Journal:** `journal.md` is append-only institutional memory. Every entry uses the full template (TL;DR, long description, what worked, what failed, what was kept/discarded, next steps) with absolute timestamps and verbatim error messages. Correct wrong past entries with a new entry referencing the old one, never by editing. Template and example: `docs/rules/journal.md`.
101	
102	**Doc pruning:** at the end of every response, do a quick pass over `docs/functions.md` — grep-check that functions you touched still exist and have callers, delete dead entries. Seconds, not minutes. Do a full audit of every entry only when the user explicitly asks for a thorough prune. This rule deletes documentation only, never source code.
103	
104	## Final Checklist
105	
106	Before declaring any task complete, verify each item. Any failure means the task is not done — fix it or report the exact blocker.
107	
108	1. `make lint` clean (format, ruff, mypy strict, documentation audit, no comments — zero warnings, zero suppressions).
109	2. `make test` passes, including the new E2E test for this change — actually run, output captured.
110	3. `make pyaot` clean (no errors, no false positives — pyaot.py was updated if needed).
111	4. New pieces were proven in `tests/` before integration, and those tests are committed.
112	5. Makefile and `requirements.txt` current if setup, run, test, or dependencies changed.
113	6. `git diff` reviewed; every changed line justified by the task.
114	7. `docs/functions.md` updated for every function added/changed/removed; stale entries pruned.
115	8. `journal.md` entry written with the full template, including test output and what was kept/discarded.
116	9. Work committed in small, plain-message commits.
117	10. The diff contains no placeholders, no comments, no ignore directives.

| Prove new code in `tests/` before integration | Restructuring `tests/`, `docs/`, or the Makefile | Reporting success with failing or unrun tests |

## Code Rules

**Real implementations only.** Every value, function, and config you write is the actual final version. No `YOUR_API_KEY`, no `example.com`, no `pass` bodies, no "replace this later". If you lack information only the user has (a credential, a decision), stop and ask rather than inventing a stand-in. Before finishing a file, search it for `TODO`, `FIXME`, `placeholder`, and stub bodies.

**No comments — document in `docs/functions.md` instead.** Source code carries meaning through names and structure alone. Every function gets a full entry in `docs/functions.md` (purpose, parameters, returns, side effects, failure modes, callers/callees, last-modified). Add the entry when you add the function, update it when you change it, delete it when you delete it — same session. Entry format and a complete example: `docs/rules/documentation.md`.

**Fully typed.** Every parameter, return value, and class attribute is annotated. `mypy --strict` passes with zero errors on everything you touch. Avoid `Any`; where it is genuinely unavoidable, explain why in the function's doc entry. Fix type errors rather than suppressing them.

**Small and flat.** Functions stay under ~40 lines and 3 levels of nesting. Use guard clauses and extraction. If a function's honest name needs the word "and", split it. Extracted helpers get doc entries and test coverage like any function.

**Naming.** Match the existing codebase conventions first. Where none exist: `snake_case` for functions, variables, and files; `PascalCase` for classes; `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` for constants. Names state intent precisely:

```python
def retry_failed_uploads(pending_jobs: list[UploadJob], timeout_seconds: float) -> list[UploadJob]:
```

not `def process2(data, t):`. Booleans read as predicates (`is_ready`), collections are plural, units go in the name when ambiguous.

**No dead code.** In files you are working on, delete unused imports, variables, unreachable branches, and functions with zero callers (verify with a repo-wide grep first). Git history is the archive — note the last commit hash in `journal.md` if it might be wanted again. Dead code in files outside your task is a journal finding, not a deletion.

**Fail loud.** Catch only specific exceptions you can genuinely handle. Don't return `None` or empty defaults to paper over a failure the caller needs to know about. Validate inputs at boundaries (CLI args, file contents, network responses) and fail there with a message stating what was expected and what was received. Every failure mode you introduce is documented in the function's doc entry and exercised by a test where practical.

**No hardcoded paths or secrets.** Secrets come from environment variables or a git-ignored `.env`; if a real secret is needed and unavailable, ask the user. Paths are computed relative to the repository root. Tunable values (paths, ports, model hyperparameters, thresholds) live in one config module with defaults sane enough that `make run` and `make test` work untouched.

## Testing Rules

The codebase is the expensive PC; `tests/` is the trash PC you try parts on first. Nothing unproven gets installed in the expensive one.

**Sandbox first.** Before a new function, dependency, or algorithm lands in a source file: write a test in `tests/` that exercises it in isolation with real inputs and real assertions, run it, see it pass, then integrate. This applies even to one-liners you are sure about. If the isolated test fails, the source tree stays untouched while you iterate in `tests/`, journaling failed attempts.

**E2E on everything.** Every change — however small — gets an end-to-end test that exercises the real entry point with real inputs, plus a real run of the suite (`make test`), with the actual output recorded in the journal. Unit tests are welcome additions, never substitutes. Failing tests mean the task is not done: fix the code, or journal the exact failure state and report it. Never delete, skip, or weaken a test to make it pass.

**Tests are permanent and committed.** Isolated proving tests go in `tests/`, end-to-end suites in `tests/e2e/`. They are regression evidence, not scratch files. Full procedure: `docs/rules/testing.md`.

## Scope Rules

Touch only the files and lines the task requires. Needing to edit `batch.py` is not license to refactor, reformat, or "clean up" `LR.py` or anything else. Before editing a file, check its dependents via the callers/callees in `docs/functions.md`; after editing, the tests prove dependents still work. No drive-by renames, reformatting of untouched code, dependency bumps, or deletions outside the task. If an out-of-scope problem genuinely blocks you, journal it and ask the user before touching it. The `git diff` review in step 8 is where you catch and revert scope creep.

## Training Script Change Rules

Whenever you edit the training script (`train.py` or anything under `src/mythosmini/`) to change training behavior, you MUST run a full 2B-token test for that change before it is accepted: `python3 train.py 2 4`, end to end through benchmarking and SLERP. One feature per test — never add two things and then test, because you will not know what did what. Each feature gets its own change, its own 2B-token run, and its own row in `scores.md` recording the commit ID, what was done, whether it is being kept or reverted, a description, and the resulting benchmark scores. A change without its 2B-token test result in `scores.md` is not done.

## Process Rules

**Commits:** commit after every small unit that leaves the repo working — many per session, never one big one at the end. Committing is your default behavior; do not wait for the user to ask. Messages are one line, lowercase, plain, stating what changed:

```
fix off-by-one in batch loader
add e2e test for tokenizer round-trip
```

No prefixes, no bullet lists, no bodies, no trailers, no emoji. Never commit a known-broken state without marking it (`wip: parser broken on empty input`) and fixing it in the next commits.

**Dependencies:** exact pins only (`torch==2.9.1`), in `requirements.txt`. Adding one means: pin the version you tested, update `make setup`, journal why it was needed. Prefer the standard library when it does the job. Upgrades are their own explicit task, never a side effect.

**Journal:** `journal.md` is append-only institutional memory. Every entry uses the full template (TL;DR, long description, what worked, what failed, what was kept/discarded, next steps) with absolute timestamps and verbatim error messages. Correct wrong past entries with a new entry referencing the old one, never by editing. Template and example: `docs/rules/journal.md`.

**Doc pruning:** at the end of every response, do a quick pass over `docs/functions.md` — grep-check that functions you touched still exist and have callers, delete dead entries. Seconds, not minutes. Do a full audit of every entry only when the user explicitly asks for a thorough prune. This rule deletes documentation only, never source code.

## Final Checklist

Before declaring any task complete, verify each item. Any failure means the task is not done — fix it or report the exact blocker.

1. `make lint` clean (format, ruff, mypy strict, documentation audit, no comments — zero warnings, zero suppressions).
2. `make test` passes, including the new E2E test for this change — actually run, output captured.
3. `make pyaot` clean (no errors, no false positives — pyaot.py was updated if needed).
4. New pieces were proven in `tests/` before integration, and those tests are committed.
5. Makefile and `requirements.txt` current if setup, run, test, or dependencies changed.
6. `git diff` reviewed; every changed line justified by the task.
7. `docs/functions.md` updated for every function added/changed/removed; stale entries pruned.
8. `journal.md` entry written with the full template, including test output and what was kept/discarded.
9. Work committed in small, plain-message commits.
10. The diff contains no placeholders, no comments, no ignore directives.

            path.stem, state, model_config, data, eval_batch, info, leaderboard, parameter_count
        )
        run_log.log({"checkpoint": path.stem, **asdict(scores)})
        candidates.append(
            MergeCandidate(
                name=path.stem,
                state=state,
                steps=frozenset({int(checkpoint["step"])}),
                scores=scores,
            )
        )
    run_log.shutdown()

def slerp_phase(
    paths: RunPaths,
    candidates: list[MergeCandidate],
    model_config: ModelConfig,
    data: BenchmarkData,
    eval_batch: int,
    info: DeviceInfo,
    leaderboard: list[LeaderboardEntry],
    parameter_count: int,
) -> MergeCandidate:
    best_seed = select_diverse(candidates, 1)[0]
    print("best checkpoint before slerp:")
    print(
        format_placement(
            best_seed.name,
            compute_placement(
                scores_to_entry(best_seed.name, parameter_count, best_seed.scores), leaderboard
            ),
        )
    )

    def evaluate(name: str, state: dict[str, Tensor]) -> BenchmarkScores:
        return benchmark_state_dict(
            name, state, model_config, data, eval_batch, info, leaderboard, parameter_count
        )

    champion = run_tournament(candidates, evaluate, print)
    champion_path = paths.merges / "champion.pt"
    torch.save(
        {"model": champion.state, "model_config": asdict(model_config), "name": champion.name},
        champion_path,

def report_final(
    champion: MergeCandidate,
    leaderboard: list[LeaderboardEntry],
    parameter_count: int,
) -> None:
    entry = scores_to_entry(champion.name, parameter_count, champion.scores)
    placement = compute_placement(entry, leaderboard)
    print("final results:")
    print(f"  champion: {champion.name}")
    print(f"  wikitext-2 byte perplexity: {champion.scores.wiki_ppl:.3f}")
    print(f"  blimp accuracy: {champion.scores.blimp:.2f}")
    print(f"  arc-easy accuracy: {champion.scores.arc:.2f}")
    print("  " + format_placement("leaderboard placement", placement))


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    token_budget, percent = parse_args(argv)
    run_dir = REPO_ROOT / "runs" / time.strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    paths = RunPaths(run_dir=run_dir)
    paths.create()
    print(f"run directory: {run_dir}")
    print(f"token budget: {token_budget}, quality percent: {percent * 100:.1f}%")
    leaderboard = fetch_leaderboard(paths.leaderboard_cache / "index.html")
    print_standings(leaderboard)
    info = detect_device()
    print(f"device: {describe_device(info)}")
    train_phase(paths, token_budget, percent, info)
    candidates, model_config, data, eval_batch, parameter_count = benchmark_phase(
        paths, info, leaderboard
    )
    champion = slerp_phase(
        paths, candidates, model_config, data, eval_batch, info, leaderboard, parameter_count
    )
    report_final(champion, leaderboard, parameter_count)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":

from pathlib import Path

import torch

from torch.nn import functional

from src.mythosmini.config import (
    CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_STEPS,

)

from src.mythosmini.training.optimizer import build_nadamw

@dataclass
class TrainerDeps:
    model: MythosMini
    model_config: ModelConfig
    train_config: TrainConfig
    buffer: SequenceBuffer
    device_info: DeviceInfo
    checkpoint_dir: Path
    saver: BackgroundSaver
    run_log: RunLog
    bar: "tqdm[None]"


@dataclass
class TrainState:
    plan: BatchPlan
    step: int = 0
    tokens_done: int = 0
    last_loss: float = 0.0
    saved_checkpoints: list[Path] = field(default_factory=list)


def compute_loss(model: MythosMini, batch: Tensor, loops: int, dtype: torch.dtype) -> Tensor:
    device_type = batch.device.type
    with torch.autocast(device_type=device_type, dtype=dtype, enabled=dtype != torch.float32):
        logits = model(batch[:, :-1], loops=loops)
        vocab = logits.shape[-1]
        return functional.cross_entropy(logits.reshape(-1, vocab), batch[:, 1:].reshape(-1))


def accumulate_gradients(
    deps: TrainerDeps, state: TrainState, loops: int, dtype: torch.dtype
) -> Tensor | None:
    while True:
        try:
            total: Tensor | None = None
            for _ in range(state.plan.grad_accum):
                batch = deps.buffer.next_batch(state.plan.micro_batch)
                if batch is None:
                    return None
                loss = compute_loss(deps.model, batch, loops, dtype)
                torch.autograd.backward(loss / state.plan.grad_accum)
                detached = loss.detach()
                total = detached if total is None else total + detached
            if total is None:
                return None
            return total / state.plan.grad_accum
        except torch.OutOfMemoryError:
            if deps.device_info.device == "cuda":
                torch.cuda.empty_cache()
            old_plan = state.plan
            state.plan = shrink_after_oom(state.plan)
            deps.model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            emit_log_line(
                deps.bar,
                f"oom at step {state.step}: micro batch {old_plan.micro_batch} -> "
                f"{state.plan.micro_batch}, grad accum {old_plan.grad_accum} -> "
                f"{state.plan.grad_accum}",

def save_checkpoint(deps: TrainerDeps, state: TrainState, optimizer: torch.optim.NAdam) -> Path:
    destination = deps.checkpoint_dir / f"step_{state.step:08d}.pt"
    payload = {
        "model": dict(deps.model.state_dict()),
        "optimizer": optimizer.state_dict(),
        "step": state.step,
        "tokens_done": state.tokens_done,
        "model_config": asdict(deps.model_config),
        "loss": state.last_loss,
    }
    deps.saver.submit(payload, destination)
    state.saved_checkpoints.append(destination)
    return destination

    message = (
        f"step {state.step} tokens {state.tokens_done} loss {state.last_loss:.4f} "
        f"lr {lr:.2e} micro_batch {state.plan.micro_batch} accum {state.plan.grad_accum}"
    )

        message += f" checkpoint {saved.name}"
    emit_log_line(deps.bar, message)

            "step": state.step,
            "tokens": state.tokens_done,
            "loss": state.last_loss,
            "lr": lr,
            "micro_batch": state.plan.micro_batch,
            "grad_accum": state.plan.grad_accum,
            "checkpoint": saved.name if saved is not None else None,
        }
    )


def run_training(deps: TrainerDeps, initial_plan: BatchPlan, token_budget: int) -> TrainState:
    config = deps.train_config
    state = TrainState(plan=initial_plan)
    optimizer = build_nadamw(deps.model, config)
    dtype = autocast_dtype(deps.device_info)
    rng = random.Random(config.seed)
    tokens_per_step = initial_plan.effective_batch * config.seq_len
    total_steps = max(1, token_budget // tokens_per_step)
    deps.model.train()
    latest_loss: Tensor | None = None
    while state.tokens_done < token_budget:
        lr = lr_at_step(state.step, total_steps, config)
        for group in optimizer.param_groups:
            group["lr"] = lr
        loops = rng.randint(config.loop_min, config.loop_max)
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        mean_loss = accumulate_gradients(deps, state, loops, dtype)
        if mean_loss is None:
            emit_log_line(deps.bar, f"data stream exhausted at step {state.step}")
            break
        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(deps.model.parameters(), config.grad_clip)
        optimizer.step()
        latest_loss = mean_loss
        state.step += 1
        step_tokens = state.plan.effective_batch * config.seq_len
        state.tokens_done += step_tokens
        deps.bar.update(step_tokens)
        should_checkpoint = state.step % CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_STEPS == 0
        if should_checkpoint or state.step % LOG_INTERVAL_STEPS == 0:
            state.last_loss = float(mean_loss.item())
            saved = save_checkpoint(deps, state, optimizer) if should_checkpoint else None
            log_progress(deps, state, lr, saved)
    if latest_loss is not None:
        state.last_loss = float(latest_loss.item())
    already_saved = state.step % CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_STEPS == 0 and state.saved_checkpoints
    if not already_saved:
        final = save_checkpoint(deps, state, optimizer)
        log_progress(deps, state, lr_at_step(state.step, total_steps, config), final)
    deps.saver.wait_for_all()
    return state

    angles = torch.outer(positions, inv_freq)
    return torch.cos(angles), torch.sin(angles)


def apply_rope(x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    seq_len = x.shape[2]
    cos_slice = cos[:seq_len].to(x.dtype)
    sin_slice = sin[:seq_len].to(x.dtype)
    x_even = x[..., 0::2]
    x_odd = x[..., 1::2]
    rotated_even = x_even * cos_slice - x_odd * sin_slice
    rotated_odd = x_even * sin_slice + x_odd * cos_slice
    return torch.stack((rotated_even, rotated_odd), dim=-1).flatten(-2)


class SwiGlu(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim: int, hidden: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.gate = nn.Linear(dim, hidden, bias=False)
        self.up = nn.Linear(dim, hidden, bias=False)
        self.down = nn.Linear(hidden, dim, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        result: Tensor = self.down(functional.silu(self.gate(x)) * self.up(x))
        return result


class Attention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.n_heads = config.n_heads
        self.head_dim = config.dim // config.n_heads
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(config.dim, 3 * config.dim, bias=False)
        self.out = nn.Linear(config.dim, config.dim, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor, qkv_delta: Tensor | None) -> Tensor:
        batch, seq_len, dim = x.shape
        qkv = self.qkv(x)
        if qkv_delta is not None:
            qkv = qkv + qkv_delta
        q, k, v = qkv.split(dim, dim=-1)
        q = q.view(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        k = k.view(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        v = v.view(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        q = apply_rope(q, cos, sin)
        k = apply_rope(k, cos, sin)
        attended = functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True)
        merged = attended.transpose(1, 2).reshape(batch, seq_len, dim)
        projected: Tensor = self.out(merged)
        return projected


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.attn_norm = nn.RMSNorm(config.dim)
        self.attn = Attention(config)
        self.ffn_norm = nn.RMSNorm(config.dim)
        self.ffn = SwiGlu(config.dim, config.ffn_hidden)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor, qkv_delta: Tensor | None) -> Tensor:
        x = x + self.attn(self.attn_norm(x), cos, sin, qkv_delta)
        result: Tensor = x + self.ffn(self.ffn_norm(x))
        return result


class LoopLora(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig, max_loops: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.down = nn.ModuleList(
            nn.Linear(config.dim, config.lora_rank, bias=False) for _ in range(max_loops)
        )
        self.up = nn.ModuleList(
            nn.Linear(config.lora_rank, 3 * config.dim, bias=False) for _ in range(max_loops)
        )
        for up in self.up:
            nn.init.zeros_(cast(nn.Linear, up).weight)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, loop_index: int) -> Tensor:
        clamped = min(loop_index, len(self.down) - 1)
        delta: Tensor = self.up[clamped](self.down[clamped](x))
        return delta


class MythosMini(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig, max_loops: int = 8) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.config = config
        self.max_loops = max_loops
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, config.dim)
        self.prelude = nn.ModuleList(Block(config) for _ in range(config.prelude_layers))
        self.shared = Block(config)
        self.loop_lora = LoopLora(config, max_loops)
        self.loop_embed = nn.Embedding(max_loops, config.dim)
        self.coda = nn.ModuleList(Block(config) for _ in range(config.coda_layers))
        self.final_norm = nn.RMSNorm(config.dim)
        cos, sin = build_rope_cache(config)
        self.register_buffer("rope_cos", cos, persistent=False)
        self.register_buffer("rope_sin", sin, persistent=False)

    def forward(self, tokens: Tensor, loops: int | None = None) -> Tensor:
        loop_count = loops if loops is not None else self.config.shared_loops
        cos = self.rope_cos
        sin = self.rope_sin
        x = self.embed(tokens)
        for block in self.prelude:
            x = block(x, cos, sin, None)
        for loop_index in range(loop_count):
            clamped = min(loop_index, self.max_loops - 1)
            gated = x + self.loop_embed.weight[clamped]
            delta = self.loop_lora(gated, loop_index)
            x = self.shared(gated, cos, sin, delta)
        for block in self.coda:
            x = block(x, cos, sin, None)
        x = self.final_norm(x)
        return functional.linear(x, self.embed.weight)


def count_parameters(model: nn.Module) -> int:
    return sum(parameter.numel() for parameter in model.parameters())

Read pipeline. Here efficiency targets, ranked by payoff.

## Big wins

**1. No `torch.compile` anywhere.** `transformer.py:116` forward runs `shared` block `loop_count` times in Python loop + prelude/coda. Hot path, never compiled. `torch.compile(model)` = biggest single speedup. Catch: `loops` varies per step (`loop.py:138` `rng.randint(2,6)`) → recompiles per loop count. Fix: `mark_dynamic` or compile the `Block`, not whole model. Worth a 2B test.

**2. Model reallocated per eval.** `benchmark_state_dict` (`train.py:135`) builds fresh `MythosMini(...).to(device)` for *every checkpoint* and *every SLERP candidate*. Tournament evals many candidates → many full allocations + CUDA init churn. Fix: build ONE model once, `load_state_dict` into it each eval. Pure waste, no accuracy risk.

**3. Optimizer state saved every checkpoint.** `save_checkpoint` (`loop.py:88`) writes `optimizer.state_dict()` every 2000 steps. NAdamW state ~= model size → doubles disk I/O. Benchmark/SLERP only read `["model"]`. If not resuming mid-run, drop optimizer from periodic checkpoints (or save only latest). Cuts saver I/O ~half.

## Medium

**4. RoPE recast every call.** `apply_rope` (`transformer.py:24`) does `cos[:seq_len].to(x.dtype)` every attention every loop. seq_len fixed (512), dtype fixed. Precompute cos/sin in autocast dtype once, slice only. Also `stack+flatten` interleave allocates 2 temps/call — `torch.cat` of halves or rotate-half layout cheaper.

**5. Benchmark every checkpoint.** `benchmark_phase` (`train.py:162`) benches ALL `step_*.pt`. With 2000-step interval over 2B tokens = many. SLERP only needs top diverse seeds. Pre-filter by cheap proxy (last-N or every-other) before full 3-dataset bench.

**6. `total` loss tensor accumulates on device.** `accumulate_gradients:70` keeps running GPU tensor sum across accum just for logging mean. Only `.item()` at log steps. Could skip sum except on log steps. Minor.

## Small
- `buffer.next_batch` `torch.cat` per batch even when one chunk — already guarded, ok. `non_blocking=True` to CUDA but source likely pageable (not pinned) → no async. Pin loader memory.
- LR loop over param_groups every step (`loop.py:136`) — negligible.

## Recommendation
Order by payoff: **#2 + #3 first** (free, no accuracy risk, no 2B test needed since output identical). Then **#1 torch.compile** (needs own 2B run per AGENTS.md rule). #4 cheap correctness-neutral win.

Want me to implement #2 and #3? Those are safe and need no full training run.

from typing import cast

import torch
from torch import Tensor, nn
from torch.nn import functional

from src.mythosmini.config import ModelConfig


def build_rope_cache(config: ModelConfig) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    head_dim = config.dim // config.n_heads
    positions = torch.arange(config.max_seq_len, dtype=torch.float32)
    inv_freq = 1.0 / (
        config.rope_base ** (torch.arange(0, head_dim, 2, dtype=torch.float32) / head_dim)
    )
    angles = torch.outer(positions, inv_freq)
    return torch.cos(angles), torch.sin(angles)


def apply_rope(x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    seq_len = x.shape[2]
    cos_slice = cos[:seq_len].to(x.dtype)
    sin_slice = sin[:seq_len].to(x.dtype)
    x_even = x[..., 0::2]
    x_odd = x[..., 1::2]
    rotated_even = x_even * cos_slice - x_odd * sin_slice
    rotated_odd = x_even * sin_slice + x_odd * cos_slice
    return torch.stack((rotated_even, rotated_odd), dim=-1).flatten(-2)


class SwiGlu(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim: int, hidden: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.gate = nn.Linear(dim, hidden, bias=False)
        self.up = nn.Linear(dim, hidden, bias=False)
        self.down = nn.Linear(hidden, dim, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        result: Tensor = self.down(functional.silu(self.gate(x)) * self.up(x))
        return result


class Attention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.n_heads = config.n_heads
        self.head_dim = config.dim // config.n_heads
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(config.dim, 3 * config.dim, bias=False)
        self.out = nn.Linear(config.dim, config.dim, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor, qkv_delta: Tensor | None) -> Tensor:
        batch, seq_len, dim = x.shape
        qkv = self.qkv(x)
        if qkv_delta is not None:
            qkv = qkv + qkv_delta
        q, k, v = qkv.split(dim, dim=-1)
        q = q.view(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        k = k.view(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        v = v.view(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        q = apply_rope(q, cos, sin)
        k = apply_rope(k, cos, sin)
        attended = functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True)
        merged = attended.transpose(1, 2).reshape(batch, seq_len, dim)
        projected: Tensor = self.out(merged)
        return projected


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.attn_norm = nn.RMSNorm(config.dim)
        self.attn = Attention(config)
        self.ffn_norm = nn.RMSNorm(config.dim)
        self.ffn = SwiGlu(config.dim, config.ffn_hidden)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor, qkv_delta: Tensor | None) -> Tensor:
        x = x + self.attn(self.attn_norm(x), cos, sin, qkv_delta)
        result: Tensor = x + self.ffn(self.ffn_norm(x))
        return result


class LoopLora(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig, max_loops: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.down = nn.ModuleList(
            nn.Linear(config.dim, config.lora_rank, bias=False) for _ in range(max_loops)
        )
        self.up = nn.ModuleList(
            nn.Linear(config.lora_rank, 3 * config.dim, bias=False) for _ in range(max_loops)
        )
        for up in self.up:
            nn.init.zeros_(cast(nn.Linear, up).weight)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, loop_index: int) -> Tensor:
        clamped = min(loop_index, len(self.down) - 1)
        delta: Tensor = self.up[clamped](self.down[clamped](x))
        return delta


class MythosMini(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig, max_loops: int = 8) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.config = config
        self.max_loops = max_loops
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, config.dim)
        self.prelude = nn.ModuleList(Block(config) for _ in range(config.prelude_layers))
        self.shared = Block(config)
        self.loop_lora = LoopLora(config, max_loops)
        self.loop_embed = nn.Embedding(max_loops, config.dim)
        self.coda = nn.ModuleList(Block(config) for _ in range(config.coda_layers))
        self.final_norm = nn.RMSNorm(config.dim)
        cos, sin = build_rope_cache(config)

from typing import cast

import torch
from torch import Tensor, nn
from torch.nn import functional

from src.mythosmini.config import ModelConfig


def build_rope_cache(config: ModelConfig) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    head_dim = config.dim // config.n_heads
    positions = torch.arange(config.max_seq_len, dtype=torch.float32)
    inv_freq = 1.0 / (
        config.rope_base ** (torch.arange(0, head_dim, 2, dtype=torch.float32) / head_dim)
    )
    angles = torch.outer(positions, inv_freq)
    return torch.cos(angles), torch.sin(angles)


def apply_rope(x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    x_even = x[..., 0::2]
    x_odd = x[..., 1::2]
    rotated_even = x_even * cos - x_odd * sin
    rotated_odd = x_even * sin + x_odd * cos
    return torch.stack((rotated_even, rotated_odd), dim=-1).flatten(-2)


class SwiGlu(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim: int, hidden: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.gate = nn.Linear(dim, hidden, bias=False)
        self.up = nn.Linear(dim, hidden, bias=False)
        self.down = nn.Linear(hidden, dim, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        result: Tensor = self.down(functional.silu(self.gate(x)) * self.up(x))
        return result


class Attention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.n_heads = config.n_heads
        self.head_dim = config.dim // config.n_heads
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(config.dim, 3 * config.dim, bias=False)
        self.out = nn.Linear(config.dim, config.dim, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor, qkv_delta: Tensor | None) -> Tensor:
        batch, seq_len, dim = x.shape
        qkv = self.qkv(x)
        if qkv_delta is not None:
            qkv = qkv + qkv_delta
        q, k, v = qkv.split(dim, dim=-1)
        q = q.view(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        k = k.view(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        v = v.view(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        q = apply_rope(q, cos, sin)
        k = apply_rope(k, cos, sin)
        attended = functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True)
        merged = attended.transpose(1, 2).reshape(batch, seq_len, dim)
        projected: Tensor = self.out(merged)
        return projected


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.attn_norm = nn.RMSNorm(config.dim)
        self.attn = Attention(config)
        self.ffn_norm = nn.RMSNorm(config.dim)
        self.ffn = SwiGlu(config.dim, config.ffn_hidden)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor, qkv_delta: Tensor | None) -> Tensor:
        x = x + self.attn(self.attn_norm(x), cos, sin, qkv_delta)
        result: Tensor = x + self.ffn(self.ffn_norm(x))
        return result


class LoopLora(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig, max_loops: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.down = nn.ModuleList(
            nn.Linear(config.dim, config.lora_rank, bias=False) for _ in range(max_loops)
        )
        self.up = nn.ModuleList(
            nn.Linear(config.lora_rank, 3 * config.dim, bias=False) for _ in range(max_loops)
        )
        for up in self.up:
            nn.init.zeros_(cast(nn.Linear, up).weight)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, loop_index: int) -> Tensor:
        clamped = min(loop_index, len(self.down) - 1)
        delta: Tensor = self.up[clamped](self.down[clamped](x))
        return delta


class MythosMini(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig, max_loops: int = 8) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.config = config
        self.max_loops = max_loops
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, config.dim)
        self.prelude = nn.ModuleList(Block(config) for _ in range(config.prelude_layers))
        self.shared = Block(config)
        self.loop_lora = LoopLora(config, max_loops)
        self.loop_embed = nn.Embedding(max_loops, config.dim)
        self.coda = nn.ModuleList(Block(config) for _ in range(config.coda_layers))
        self.final_norm = nn.RMSNorm(config.dim)
        cos, sin = build_rope_cache(config)
        self.register_buffer("rope_cos", cos, persistent=False)
        self.register_buffer("rope_sin", sin, persistent=False)

    def forward(self, tokens: Tensor, loops: int | None = None) -> Tensor:
        loop_count = loops if loops is not None else self.config.shared_loops
        cos = self.rope_cos
        sin = self.rope_sin
        x = self.embed(tokens)
        for block in self.prelude:
            x = block(x, cos, sin, None)
        for loop_index in range(loop_count):
            clamped = min(loop_index, self.max_loops - 1)
            gated = x + self.loop_embed.weight[clamped]
            delta = self.loop_lora(gated, loop_index)
            x = self.shared(gated, cos, sin, delta)
        for block in self.coda:
            x = block(x, cos, sin, None)
        x = self.final_norm(x)
        return functional.linear(x, self.embed.weight)

    return sum(parameter.numel() for parameter in model.parameters())

from typing import cast

import torch
from torch import Tensor, nn
from torch.nn import functional

from src.mythosmini.config import ModelConfig


def build_rope_cache(config: ModelConfig) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    head_dim = config.dim // config.n_heads
    positions = torch.arange(config.max_seq_len, dtype=torch.float32)
    inv_freq = 1.0 / (
        config.rope_base ** (torch.arange(0, head_dim, 2, dtype=torch.float32) / head_dim)
    )
    angles = torch.outer(positions, inv_freq)
    return torch.cos(angles), torch.sin(angles)


def apply_rope(x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    x_even = x[..., 0::2]
    x_odd = x[..., 1::2]
    rotated_even = x_even * cos - x_odd * sin
    rotated_odd = x_even * sin + x_odd * cos
    return torch.stack((rotated_even, rotated_odd), dim=-1).flatten(-2)


class SwiGlu(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim: int, hidden: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.gate = nn.Linear(dim, hidden, bias=False)
        self.up = nn.Linear(dim, hidden, bias=False)
        self.down = nn.Linear(hidden, dim, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        result: Tensor = self.down(functional.silu(self.gate(x)) * self.up(x))
        return result


class Attention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.n_heads = config.n_heads
        self.head_dim = config.dim // config.n_heads
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(config.dim, 3 * config.dim, bias=False)
        self.out = nn.Linear(config.dim, config.dim, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor, qkv_delta: Tensor | None) -> Tensor:
        batch, seq_len, dim = x.shape
        qkv = self.qkv(x)
        if qkv_delta is not None:
            qkv = qkv + qkv_delta
        q, k, v = qkv.split(dim, dim=-1)
        q = q.view(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        k = k.view(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        v = v.view(batch, seq_len, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
        q = apply_rope(q, cos, sin)
        k = apply_rope(k, cos, sin)
        attended = functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True)
        merged = attended.transpose(1, 2).reshape(batch, seq_len, dim)
        projected: Tensor = self.out(merged)
        return projected


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.attn_norm = nn.RMSNorm(config.dim)
        self.attn = Attention(config)
        self.ffn_norm = nn.RMSNorm(config.dim)
        self.ffn = SwiGlu(config.dim, config.ffn_hidden)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, cos: Tensor, sin: Tensor, qkv_delta: Tensor | None) -> Tensor:
        x = x + self.attn(self.attn_norm(x), cos, sin, qkv_delta)
        result: Tensor = x + self.ffn(self.ffn_norm(x))
        return result


class LoopLora(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig, max_loops: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.down = nn.ModuleList(
            nn.Linear(config.dim, config.lora_rank, bias=False) for _ in range(max_loops)
        )
        self.up = nn.ModuleList(
            nn.Linear(config.lora_rank, 3 * config.dim, bias=False) for _ in range(max_loops)
        )
        for up in self.up:
            nn.init.zeros_(cast(nn.Linear, up).weight)

    def forward(self, x: Tensor, loop_index: int) -> Tensor:
        clamped = min(loop_index, len(self.down) - 1)
        delta: Tensor = self.up[clamped](self.down[clamped](x))
        return delta


class MythosMini(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: ModelConfig, max_loops: int = 8) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.config = config
        self.max_loops = max_loops
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, config.dim)
        self.prelude = nn.ModuleList(Block(config) for _ in range(config.prelude_layers))
        self.shared = Block(config)
        self.loop_lora = LoopLora(config, max_loops)
        self.loop_embed = nn.Embedding(max_loops, config.dim)
        self.coda = nn.ModuleList(Block(config) for _ in range(config.coda_layers))
        self.final_norm = nn.RMSNorm(config.dim)
        cos, sin = build_rope_cache(config)
        self.register_buffer("rope_cos", cos, persistent=False)
        self.register_buffer("rope_sin", sin, persistent=False)

    def forward(self, tokens: Tensor, loops: int | None = None) -> Tensor:
        loop_count = loops if loops is not None else self.config.shared_loops
        x = self.embed(tokens)
        device_type = tokens.device.type
        compute_dtype = (
            torch.get_autocast_dtype(device_type)
            if torch.is_autocast_enabled(device_type)
            else x.dtype
        )
        seq_len = tokens.shape[1]
        cos = self.rope_cos[:seq_len].to(compute_dtype)
        sin = self.rope_sin[:seq_len].to(compute_dtype)
        for block in self.prelude:
            x = block(x, cos, sin, None)
        for loop_index in range(loop_count):
            clamped = min(loop_index, self.max_loops - 1)
            gated = x + self.loop_embed.weight[clamped]
            delta = self.loop_lora(gated, loop_index)
            x = self.shared(gated, cos, sin, delta)
        for block in self.coda:
            x = block(x, cos, sin, None)
        x = self.final_norm(x)
        return functional.linear(x, self.embed.weight)


def count_parameters(model: nn.Module) -> int:
    return sum(parameter.numel() for parameter in model.parameters())
